source_edges: LevelSavegame::__SaveObjects 0x462d84 walks the existing ObjectManager map in signed-key order, applies ObjectBase+0x28 and online/player gates, writes name +0x5c, manager key, type +0x64, then calls virtual Serialize +0x10 and patches the payload length.

LevelSavegame::__LoadObjects 0x461e90 resolves the already-loaded object by ObjectManager key/name, calls virtual Deserialize +0x14, and seeks to the recorded payload end if the virtual reader consumes a different length. It does not construct an ItemObject from an item id.

ItemManager::PreCache 0x3eb6e4 creates five source ObjectManager objects named ItemObject_%02u_%02u per ItemAudioVisual category and calls ItemObject::InitOnce 0x3ece80, then DeSpawn 0x3eac34. Spawn 0x3eacd0 rotates one of those stable shells, sets position/destination, invokes InitAgain 0x3ec0f0, enables it, and marks its pool row active.

ItemObject has no Serialize override in the pinned function inventory; the serializer contract groups Item under GameObject. GameObject::Serialize 0x38b9e4 writes ObjectBase flags +0x80/+0x8a then GameObject +0x270. GameObject::Deserialize 0x38b91c reads +0x270, asserts it equals the already-loaded object's spawnProbRolled value, and syncs visibility.
world_item_persistence_boundary.selected_port_gap: No ItemObject serializer bridge is required by the pinned source OBJS eligibility gate: ItemObject shells are not opted into the save list. NativeWorldItem/native_item_manager_pool_v1 therefore need not fabricate ObjectBase bytes or source ObjectManager identity for serialization. The exact original-engine factory/shell bridge remains a separate gameplay-parity gap, not a level-save blocker.
world_item_persistence_boundary.factory_and_shell_boundary: object_creation_map_v1 resolves source type Item to GetNewInstance<ItemObject> thunk 0x340d38, but it is dispatch metadata only; the header explicitly leaves production construction to a class-specific owner. object_manager_runtime_owner_v1 can reserve a stable signed handle/name and retain a semantic GameObject identity, but explicitly implements no source factory, ObjectHandle resolution, or ObjectBase storage. item_manager_pool_v1 is the existing single canonical V4 association/round-robin owner: its active slot binds stable NativeWorldItem identity to the V4 Item pointer and tracks the five-slot cursor, but allocates projection shells lazily and has no ObjectManager name/key or ItemObject InitOnce owner. `source_handle_ledger_v1` shell rows are fixtures only, not live Item factory receipts.
world_item_persistence_boundary.first_missing_provider: None for Item OBJS save/load: the source gate excludes these shells. If original-engine ItemObject factory parity is pursued, it still needs an executable ObjectManager::Spawn('Item') factory and retained five-shell ItemManager owner; current semantic handle and V4 projection owners are not that source runtime.
world_item_persistence_boundary.resume_assessment: The GL/EGL restore path can reuse the still-live Player V4 world_items vector and recreate NativeWorldItem physics projections through ensure_native_world_items. Terminal Level teardown clears native_world_items and its pool; no selected LevelSavegame OBJS load/save path snapshots or restores those V4 world items. This is an in-process renderer/session restore only, not level unload/reload or durable world persistence.
world_item_persistence_boundary.evidence_scope: Static IDA decompilation of the pinned ARMv7 ELF. Constructor/lifecycle details are source-field evidence; no live original ItemObject save/load capture is claimed.

source_edges: LevelSavegame::__SaveObjects gates every row on ObjectBase byte +0x28 being nonzero before it writes the object header or calls Serialize.

ObjectBase constructor 0x33f310 initializes byte +0x28 to 0. ItemObject constructor 0x3ec324 and GameObject constructor 0x38c398 do not set it; the only ItemObject-family stores found at this offset are the base initialization and GameObject::InitPost's conditional clear.
GameObject::DeclareProperties 0x38cee8 binds +0x15c to skip_checkpoint. GameObject::InitPost 0x38be5c clears +0x28 when skip_checkpoint is set. It never sets +0x28 true.

Contrasting save-enabled classes set +0x28 true in their constructors (for example Container 0x3a0810, Trigger 0x39904c, and Door 0x3e83b4). ItemManager PreCache creates ItemObject shells through ItemObject's own constructor/InitOnce path, which has no such opt-in.
item_shell_save_eligibility.port_conclusion: Pre-cached and spawned ItemObject shells remain outside LevelSavegame OBJS under the observed source lifecycle. Building an ObjectBase serializer bridge for NativeWorldItem would invent save eligibility and identity; do not implement that bridge. Current V4 inventory/profile save remains the relevant persistence owner after pickup. A separate world-item checkpoint persistence owner is not evidenced by ItemManager (its source function inventory contains only constructor, PreCache, Spawn, DeSpawn, and Flush).
item_shell_save_eligibility.evidence_scope: Static pinned ARMv7 ELF decompilation plus scoped instruction scan for ObjectBase +0x28 stores in ObjectBase/GameObject/ItemObject functions; no runtime save capture claimed.

property_write_evidence: The pinned writeAs<CharacterProperties> passes sizeof(T)=900 directly to the stream virtual write. The load path calls Object::Deserialize virtual +0x14 for the bounded OBJS payload; Character::Deserialize then readAs<CharacterProperties> passes 900 bytes directly to stream virtual read at offsets +0x8ec and +0xff4. The first word is therefore overwritten as part of the copied image; no pointer relocation/fixup or skip is present in these routines. Each image contains the original ARM32 vtable word plus 224 int32 property words. A port PropertyState sheet is only the 896-byte value payload and cannot safely stand in for this image; a relocatable source-compatible image is not established, so production serialization must remain gated.

character_property_image_lifecycle.observation: Character construction initializes the distinct runtime CharProperties owner at Character+0x560; it does not construct either Structs::CharacterProperties image at +0x8ec or +0xff4. InitAll delegates through virtual calls, InitSpawned updates spawn/state fields, and InitPost/InitFinal use the runtime owner; none creates or repairs those image headers. _LoadFromCharTable copies 0x380 bytes from row+4 to destination+4, deliberately leaving the destination's first word untouched. Therefore these source lifecycle routines provide neither a safe ARM32 vtable for a port-built image nor a way to relocate the raw deserialized image. Keep non-player Character save fail-closed; player saves omit both images by source design and remain eligible when their other providers are complete.

fixture_scope: Host regression synthesizes provider field spans to verify emitted order/length and fail-closed behavior. It does not claim a live original-runtime serialization capture. Original function sizes and hashes pin the static ELF evidence.
